question: Does compiling the PowerShell/Add-Type worker to a .exe remove the ~2s cold cost?
method: tools/lab/a2a/bench-gdi.ps1 inside WIN11-VM: start worker, send "A" on stdin, keep stdin OPEN (as the agent does), measure until 1000 bytes arrive on stdout

e2e_first_frame_ms.note: Sessions on a prewarmed agent: the worker spawn is NOT on the critical path, so exe and ps1 are indistinguishable here (466-656ms band).

engine_proof.note: Content-hashed filename: an in-place update never hits EBUSY on a running worker.

fallback_proof.how: icacls /deny <user>:(RX) on the materialized exe, then agent restart

finding_negative.what: Killing the worker mid-life is NOT a cold start
finding_negative.why: main.js 'exit' handler drops to the Chromium path and recreates its capture window; the engine swap does not address that path
finding_negative.implication: The remaining worst case (~5s) lives in the Chromium recovery/window path, not in Add-Type. That is the next target if the worst case must shrink.

limitation: The exact cold race (session arriving between registration and prewarm) could not be reproduced with the current tools: /api/relay/request returns 503 target_offline while the agent is still booting.
